title: UK 13 A plug: tighten loose cable and cord grip
diagnosis: The cable is probably pulling out because the cord grip screws have worked loose or the grip isn't clamping the grey outer sheath. I'll have you unplug it, open it, check the wires are secure, and re-tighten the cord grip.
safety_notes: Switch off at the wall and unplug before touching the plug.
Never open a plug that is still in a socket.
If you see scorching, melting, cracks or damaged wires, stop and replace the plug or cable.

steps.title: Unplug the plug
steps.instruction: Switch off at the wall socket and pull the plug fully out. The plug must never be in a socket while its cover is off.
steps.expected_visual_state: The plug is held in your hand, completely out of the wall socket, with the socket switch off.
common_mistakes: Pulling on the cable instead of the plug body
Leaving the plug in the socket while opening it

steps.title: Remove the cover screw
steps.instruction: Undo the central cross-head screw fully. Put it somewhere it can't roll away.
steps.expected_visual_state: The cover screw is out and sitting on the table next to the plug.
common_mistakes: Using the wrong size screwdriver and damaging the screw head

steps.title: Lift off the cover
steps.instruction: Lift the back cover away to expose the terminals, fuse and cord grip.
steps.expected_visual_state: The cover is off and the open tray shows three wires, the fuse and the cord grip.
common_mistakes: Prying with a metal tool and cracking the plastic
Tugging the cable while lifting the cover

steps.title: Check the wires and terminals
steps.instruction: Look at each wire under its terminal screw. Make sure brown is at live, blue at neutral and green-and-yellow at earth, with no bare copper showing outside the terminals.
steps.expected_visual_state: Brown wire sits under the right terminal by the fuse, blue under the left, green-and-yellow under the top, all with no stray strands.
common_mistakes: Mixing up the wire colours when re-seating one
Over-tightening and cutting through the wire strands
Ignoring scorch marks or damaged insulation, which means replacing the plug

steps.title: Re-seat the cable in the cord grip
steps.instruction: Loosen the two cord grip screws and position the grey outer sheath under the bar. The sheath, not the coloured wires, must be clamped.
steps.expected_visual_state: The grey sheath runs under the cord grip bar, with the coloured wires beyond it and slightly slack.
common_mistakes: Clamping the individual wires rather than the sheath
Leaving the wires pulled tight so a tug strains the terminals

steps.title: Tighten the cord grip
steps.instruction: Tighten both cord grip screws evenly until the cable can't be pulled or twisted. Give the cable a gentle tug to test it.
steps.expected_visual_state: The cord grip is flat and snug on the sheath, and the cable stays put when gently tugged.
common_mistakes: Tightening only one screw so the bar sits crooked

steps.title: Close the cover and test
steps.instruction: Refit the cover, tighten the cover screw, and only then plug it in. Gently tug the cable to confirm it is firmly held, then check the appliance works.
steps.expected_visual_state: The cover is closed and flush with the cover screw tight. The cable doesn't move when tugged and the appliance powers on.
common_mistakes: Plugging in before the cover is screwed on
Trapping the cable under the cover edge
